The '''2025–26 season''' was the [[List of Manchester City F.C. seasons|131st season]] in the existence of [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City Football Club]] and their 24th consecutive season in the [[English football league system|top flight]] of [[Football in England|English football]]. In addition to the [[2025–26 Premier League|domestic league]], Manchester City also participated in the [[2025–26 FA Cup|FA Cup]], [[2025–26 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]] and [[2025–26 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]], entering the latter for the 15th consecutive season.

This was the club's first season since [[2014–15 Manchester City F.C. season|2014–15]] without midfielder [[Kevin De Bruyne]], who departed for [[SSC Napoli|Napoli]] following the expiration of his contract, and the first season since [[2016–17 Manchester City F.C. season|2016–17]] without [[Kyle Walker]] (to [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]]) and [[Ederson (footballer, born 1993)|Ederson]] (to [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (football)|Fenerbahçe]]). [[Bernardo Silva]] was named as the club's new [[Captain (association football)|captain]] after Walker's departure. This also marked the first campaign since [[2020–21 Manchester City F.C. season|2020–21]] which Manchester City did not enter as reigning Premier League champions.

On 17 March, City were beaten 5–1 on aggregate by [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in the last 16 of the Champions League to end their participation in this season's competition. On 22 March, they won 2–0 against [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] to win the [[2026 EFL Cup final|EFL Cup]] for the first time in five seasons. [[Pep Guardiola]] also became the first manager to win the competition on five occasions. On 16 May, City won 1–0 against [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], to win their eighth [[2026 FA Cup final|FA Cup]] title in a record-breaking fourth consecutive final appearance. On 19 May, a 1–1 draw away to [[AFC Bournemouth|Bournemouth]] in their penultimate game of the season meant City ended their title race as league runners-up to Arsenal.

On 22 May, the club announced that Pep Guardiola would be stepping down as manager at the end of the season after ten years. At the time, he was the club's most successful manager in their history.

==Season summary==
===Pre-season===
The revamped [[2025 FIFA Club World Cup]] spanned the period between the 2024–25 and 2025–26 English football seasons. City's involvement in this competition is documented on their [[2024–25 Manchester City F.C. season|2024–25 season]] page.

It had been anticipated that City's squad would need a major overhaul in the summer to remain competitive at the highest level after a trophyless season. While this transition began in the previous January transfer window, further changes were expected, particularly in midfield, at full-back and potentially at centre-half if the club chose to offload some of their aging and injury-prone players. Between 9 and 11 June, the transfers of left-back [[Rayan Aït-Nouri]] from [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]]; midfielders [[Tijjani Reijnders]] from [[AC Milan|Milan]] and [[Rayan Cherki]] from [[FC Lyon|Lyon]]; and of back-up goalkeeper [[Marcus Bettinelli]] from [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] were duly completed in time for the players to join the squad for the Club World Cup at a total estimated cost of £112 million.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" /> Goalkeeper and former [[Manchester City F.C. Under-21s and Academy|Manchester City EDS]] player [[James Trafford]] also rejoined the club from [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]] for £31 million, after the Club World Cup.<ref name=":4" /> Key departures included [[Jack Grealish]], who was sent on loan to [[Everton F.C.|Everton]].<ref name=":5" /> The full squad regrouped for pre-season training at the City Football Academy on 28 July 2025. Fans were welcomed back through a ''City Are Back'' open training session at Joie Stadium on 5 August, providing supporters the first chance to see the new signings in action.<ref name="mcfc-opentraining">{{cite web |title=City Are Back: Everything you need to know about our Open Training event |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/club/city-are-back-everything-you-need-to-know-63889656 |publisher=Manchester City FC |date=1 August 2025 |access-date=20 September 2025}}</ref>

On 7 July 2025, Manchester City announced a friendly against sister club [[Palermo FC|Palermo]] to contest the inaugural Anglo-Palermitan Trophy. On 2 August, a behind-closed-doors friendly at the City Football Academy against [[Preston North End F.C.|Preston North End]] was played, ending in a 1–0 win thanks to a goal from [[Rico Lewis]]. On 9 August, City's single open, full-match friendly against Palermo resulted in a convincing 3–0 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mumford |first=Jack |title=City see off Palermo challenge to win Anglo Palermitan Trophy |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/City%20see%20off%20Palermo%20challenge%20to%20win%20Anglo%20Palermitan%20Trophy |access-date=2025-08-30 |website=Manchester City FC |language=en}}</ref>

===Start of season===
Manchester City launched their [[2025–26 Premier League|league campaign]] with an emphatic 4–0 away victory over [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] at [[Molineux Stadium|Molineux]] on 16 August 2025. [[Erling Haaland]] continued his tradition of scoring on opening days, netting a brace with goals in the 34th and 61st minutes. [[Tijjani Reijnders]], making his Premier League debut, scored one and was instrumental in both of Haaland's goals–delivering a dynamic and influential performance.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wolverhampton Wanderers v Manchester City {{!}} 2025/2026 {{!}} Premier League {{!}} Overview |url=https://www.premierleague.com/en/match/2561901 |access-date=2025-08-30 |website=www.premierleague.com |language=en}}</ref>

City next faced [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] at the City of Manchester Stadium on 23 August. Tottenham secured a 2–0 victory, with goals from [[Brennan Johnson]] in the 35th minute and [[João Palhinha]] in first-half stoppage time(45+2). Tottenham's disciplined defence and pressing game under their new manager [[Thomas Frank (football manager)|Thomas Frank]] proved decisive.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Manchester City v Tottenham Hotspur {{!}} 2025/2026 {{!}} Premier League {{!}} Overview |url=https://www.premierleague.com/en/match/2561912 |access-date=2025-08-30 |website=www.premierleague.com |language=en}}</ref>

On 31 August, Manchester City suffered a 2–1 defeat to [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]] at the [[Falmer Stadium|American Express Community Stadium]] in the Premier League.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brighton and Hove Albion v Manchester City {{!}} 2025/2026 {{!}} Premier League {{!}} Overview |url=https://www.premierleague.com/en/match/2561916/brighton-and-hove-albion-vs-manchester-city |access-date=2025-09-13 |website=www.premierleague.com |language=en}}</ref> Despite taking the lead through Erling Haaland in the 34th minute—his 88th goal in 100 league appearances—City were undone in the second half. Former Blue, [[James Milner]], equalised from the penalty spot in the 67th minute after a hand-ball from [[Matheus Nunes]], and [[Brajan Gruda]] netted the winner in the 89th minute following a late surge by Brighton. The loss marked City's second consecutive league defeat, raising concerns about their early-season form.

On transfer deadline day, 1 September 2025, Manchester City concluded several significant moves. The most notable was the signing of Italian goalkeeper [[Gianluigi Donnarumma]] from [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]] for £26 million,<ref name=":6" /> intended to succeed [[Ederson (footballer, born 1993)|Ederson]], who departed for [[Fenerbahçe S.K.|Fenerbahçe]] after eight seasons at the club.<ref name=":7" /> Other key exits included [[İlkay Gündoğan]] to [[Galatasaray S.K.|Galatasaray]] and [[Manuel Akanji]] on loan to [[Inter Milan]].<ref name=":8" /><ref name=":9" />

Following the September 2025 [[FIFA International Match Calendar|international break]], Manchester City recorded consecutive victories. On 14 September, City defeated [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] 3–0 at home in the Premier League, with goals from [[Phil Foden]] and a brace from Erling Haaland.<ref name="reuters-derby">{{cite news |first=Lori|last=Ewing|title=Man City and Haaland clobber United 3–0 in Manchester derby |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/man-city-haaland-clobber-united-3-0-manchester-derby-2025-09-14/ |publisher=Reuters |date=14 September 2025 |access-date=20 September 2025}}</ref> Four days later, on 18 September 2025, City beat [[S.S.C. Napoli|Napoli]] 2–0 in their opening [[2025–26 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]] league stage match. Haaland scored his 50th goal in the competition in his 49th appearance, becoming the fastest player to reach the milestone, while [[Jérémy Doku]] added the second against the Italian side, who played most of the match with ten men.<ref name="reuters-napoli">{{cite news |first=Lori|last=Ewing|title=Haaland nets landmark goal as City beat 10-man Napoli in Champions League |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/haaland-nets-landmark-goal-city-beat-10-man-napoli-champions-league-2025-09-18/ |publisher=Reuters |date=18 September 2025 |access-date=20 September 2025}}</ref>

===Autumn period===
Manchester City resumed their league campaign on 21 September with a 1–1 draw at [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]]. Erling Haaland put City ahead after nine minutes, but Gabriel Martinelli's stoppage-time equaliser(90+3) rescued a point for the hosts.<ref>{{cite web |title=Martinelli but then winning it with a fabulous volley from foden snatches 3 points for Arsenal in 2-1 win with Manchester City |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/martinelli-snatches-late-point-arsenal-1-1-draw-with-man-city-2025-09-21/ |website=Reuters |date=21 September 2025 |access-date=29 September 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=City denied victory by late Gunners equaliser |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/arsenal-v-manchester-city-match-report-21-september-63894065 |website=Manchester City F.C. |date=21 September 2025 |access-date=29 September 2025}}</ref> Three days later, on 24 September 2025, City advanced in the [[2025–26 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]] with a 2–0 victory over [[Huddersfield Town F.C.|Huddersfield Town]] in the third round, as Phil Foden opened the scoring and [[Savinho]] doubled the lead.<ref>{{cite web |title=Phil Foden pulls strings as Manchester City outclass Huddersfield in Carabao Cup |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/sep/24/carabao-cup-third-round-huddersfield-manchester-city-match-report |website=The Guardian |date=24 September 2025 |access-date=29 September 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Foden, Savinho score as Man City ease past Huddersfield |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/758198 |website=ESPN |date=24 September 2025 |access-date=29 September 2025}}</ref> This was followed up with an emphatic 5–1 Premier League victory over Burnley on 27 September. The match featured two own goals from [[Maxime Estève]], an injury time brace from Haaland, and a strike from Matheus Nunes, while Rico Lewis marked his 100th senior appearance for the club.<ref>{{cite web |title=Estève scores two own goals as Burnley lose 5-1 to Man City; Haaland nets twice |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/esteve-scores-two-own-goals-burnley-lose-5-1-man-city-haaland-nets-twice-2025-09-27/ |website=Reuters |date=27 September 2025 |access-date=29 September 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=City cruise to victory over Burnley |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/manchester-city-v-burnley-premier-league-match-report-27-september-2025 |website=Manchester City F.C. |date=27 September 2025 |access-date=29 September 2025}}</ref> This result left City in seventh place and five points behind early leaders and defending champions [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]].

In their second match of the Champions League league phase, City drew [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]] 2–2 away from home.<ref name="UCLMonaco2025">{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/ce84elp06wpt|title=Monaco hold Manchester City to draw in Champions League group stage|date=2 October 2025|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=29 October 2025}}</ref> Erling Haaland opened the scoring in the 15th minute, before [[Jordan Teze]] equalised three minutes later. Despite City taking a 2–1 lead into half-time thanks to another Haaland header, they were unable to maintain their advantage as [[Eric Dier]] converted a late penalty to secure a point for Monaco.

A further Haaland goal and a 1–0 away win at [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]] on 5 October meant City went into the second international break in fifth place, just three points behind new league leaders Arsenal. Haaland's 12 goals in nine appearances so far this season had elevated him to the top of the [[European Golden Shoe]] standings alongside [[Harry Kane]] and [[Kylian Mbappé]], and into the list of the [[List of Manchester City F.C. records and statistics#Player records|top 10 all-time City goalscorers]] after just over three seasons at the club.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-10-11 |title=Erling Haaland: Man City striker hot favourite for Golden Boot |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cdjz1py0xg7o |access-date=2025-10-14 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

Returning to domestic competition, City extended their winning run with a 2–0 home victory over [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] on 19 October, with Haaland reaching double figures for league goals.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hafez |first=Shamoon |title=Man City 2-0 Everton: Erling Haaland scores twice as City go second |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cgkzyply0zxt |access-date=2025-10-29 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> Three days later, City recorded another 2–0 win away to [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]], moving into seventh place in the Champions League league standings.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hafez |first=Shamoon |title=Haaland scores again as Man City end winless away run |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/clykvkez43yt |access-date=2025-10-29 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> At this point, Haaland had scored in 12 consecutive appearances for club and country. This streak, and the club's winning streak, ended soon after with a 1–0 away defeat to [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]], marking the third consecutive season that City had lost this fixture.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hafez |first=Shamoon |title=Aston Villa 1-0 Man City: Matty Cash scores winner |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c07mzp87xr8t |access-date=2025-10-29 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> By the end of October, City sat fifth in the Premier League table, six points behind leaders Arsenal.<ref name="TableOct2025">{{cite web |title=Premier League Table – October 2025 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/tables |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=29 October 2025}}</ref>

The Blues started November with a 3–1 win against [[AFC Bournemouth|Bournemouth]] at home, with Haaland pushing his goal tally to 13 in the Premier League. In the second half, [[Nico O'Reilly]] registered his first goal of the season with a composed left foot shot into the bottom right corner. Before the November international break, City defeated Liverpool 3–0 at the Etihad Stadium in what was Pep Guardiola's 1000th game in football management. Although Erling Haaland's early penalty was saved by Georgian backup goalkeeper [[Giorgi Mamardashvili]], he later opened the scoring with a header. [[Nico González (footballer, born 2002)|Nico González]] and Jérémy Doku added further goals from outside the penalty area. The result left City second in the league standings, four points behind leaders Arsenal.<ref>{{cite web |title=Man City ease to 3-0 win over Liverpool as Guardiola celebrates 1,000th game in style |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/man-city-ease-3-0-win-over-liverpool-guardiola-celebrates-1000th-game-style-2025-11-09/ |website=Reuters |date=9 November 2025 |access-date=11 November 2025}}</ref>

After the November international break, Manchester City returned to Premier League action with a 1–2 away defeat to [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]]. A long-range strike from [[Harvey Barnes]] in the 63rd minute put Newcastle ahead, but [[Rúben Dias]] equalised shortly afterwards with a volley. City's hope of a comeback ended when Barnes struck again in the 70th minute, with the goal confirmed only after a VAR review for offside.<ref>{{cite web |last1= |first1= |title=Newcastle 2-1 Man City – Premier League Match Report |website=ESPN UK |date=22 November 2025 |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/report/_/gameId/740712}}</ref>

In the Champions League, City lost 0–2 at home to [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]]. Guardiola made ten changes to his starting XI for the match, and the German side took the lead through [[Álex Grimaldo]] in the 23rd minute, with [[Patrik Schick]] doubling the advantage early in the second half to complete a surprise win.<ref>{{cite web |last1= |first1= |title=Man City 0-2 Leverkusen – Champions League Match Report |website=ESPN UK |date=25 November 2025 |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/report/_/gameId/757730}}</ref>

The Blues responded with a 3–2 victory over [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]]. Phil Foden scored after just one minute, and then struck again in stoppage time to prevent a Leeds comeback and secure all three points for City.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Foden scores injury-time winner as Man City see off Leeds fightback|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cx238r1xng2t|website=BBC Sport|access-date=2025-11-30|language=en}}</ref>

===Christmas and New Year period===
City began their busy December schedule with a 5–4 away win against [[Fulham]] at [[Craven Cottage]] on 2 December 2025. Erling Haaland scored his 100th Premier League goal — becoming the fastest player to reach that mark in just 111 appearances — and Phil Foden scored twice as City moved within two points of the league leaders, before holding on following a late Fulham fightback after they had led by four goals.<ref>{{cite_web|title=Fulham 4-5 Manchester City: Nine goals as Pep Guardiola’s side survive remarkable fightback and Erling Haaland reaches record century|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/13477810/fulham-4-5-man-city-nine-goals-as-pep-guardiolos-side-survive-remarkable-fightback-and-erling-haaland-reaches-record-century|website=Sky Sports|date=3 December 2025|access-date=14 December 2025}}</ref>

On 6 December, City recorded a 3–0 home win over [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]] in the Premier League, with goals from Rúben Dias, Joško Gvardiol and Phil Foden, narrowing the gap to the top of the table.<ref>{{cite_web|title=Manchester City 3-0 Sunderland – Highlights & Report|url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/match/_/gameId/740736/sunderland-manchester-city|website=ESPN|date=6 December 2025|access-date=14 December 2025}}</ref>

In the Champions League on 10 December, the Blues secured a 2–1 victory at Real Madrid in the league phase, coming from behind with an equaliser from Nico O'Reilly and a Haaland penalty to take the win at the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium|Santiago Bernabéu]].<ref>{{cite_web|title=Manchester City rally to beat Real Madrid 2-1 at Bernabéu|url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/manchester-city-rally-beat-real-madrid-2-1-bernabeu-2025-12-10/|website=Reuters|date=10 December 2025|access-date=14 December 2025}}</ref>

On 14 December, Manchester City continued their Premier League campaign with a 3–0 away win against [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]], with Haaland scoring twice and Foden adding a goal to keep pressure on league leaders Arsenal.<ref>{{cite_web|title=Man City keep pressure on Arsenal with 3-0 win at Palace|url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/man-city-keep-pressure-arsenal-with-3-0-win-palace-2025-12-14/|website=Reuters|date=14 December 2025|access-date=14 December 2025}}</ref>

City's festive run concluded with mixed results at the start of 2026. A 0–0 draw away to Sunderland on New Year's Day halted their winning momentum after eight consecutive victories in all competitions; before two consecutive 1–1 home draws against Chelsea and Brighton on 4 January and 7 January respectively saw City drop further ground in the title race; conceding a 94th-minute equaliser in the former fixture. Despite scoring first and dominating possession and territory in both games, Guardiola's side were unable to convert their chances, leaving them second in the Premier League table, six points behind leaders Arsenal after 21 matches. Preparations also continued for the upcoming EFL Cup semi-final against Newcastle United, following December's 2–0 quarter-final victory over Brentford.

Off the pitch, the club were rumoured to be active in the winter transfer window, reaching agreement to sign in form Ghanaian winger [[Antoine Semenyo]] from [[AFC Bournemouth|Bournemouth]] for his short-term £65 million release fee, a deal which was concluded on 9 January;<ref name="Semenyo" /> and were rumoured to also be in discussions to sign England defender [[Marc Guéhi]] from [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]]. A deal that had been predicated by long-term injuries to first-choice centre-halves [[Rúben Dias]] and [[Joško Gvardiol]] in the Chelsea game.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Jackson |first=Jamie |last2=Aarons |first2=Ed |last3=Steinberg |first3=Jacob |date=2026-01-05 |title=Manchester City weigh up move for Guéhi after Gvardiol breaks shinbone |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jan/05/manchester-city-weigh-up-move-for-palaces-guehi-after-injuries-to-gvardiol-and-dias |access-date=2026-01-09 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> That deal was concluded on 19 January for a reported £20 million fee.<ref name="Guehi" />

Semenyo immediately made his City debut on 10 January in a 10–1 FA Cup third‑round victory over [[Exeter City F.C.|Exeter City]], scoring and assisting in his first appearance — the first City player to do so since [[Sergio Agüero]] against [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]] in 2011. In all, seven different City players made goal contributions in the match, including a debut senior goal for [[Ryan McAidoo]] and a first senior goal for [[Max Alleyne]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Egerton |first=Nathan |date=2026-01-10 |title=Antoine Semenyo matches Sergio Aguero stat with DREAM Man City debut in FA Cup win |url=https://www.teamtalk.com/manchester-city/antoine-semenyo-matches-sergio-aguero-stat-with-dream-man-city-debut-in-emphatic-fa-cup-win |access-date=2026-01-11 |website=TEAMtalk |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Hafez |first=Shamoon |title=Man City 10-1 Exeter: Antoine Semenyo scores on debut |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c0lxgy7253zt |access-date=2026-01-11 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

Following their FA Cup victory, City's inconsistent January form continued. On 13 January, Guardiola's side secured a 2–0 away win over Newcastle United in the EFL Cup semi‑finals first leg, taking control of the tie through a disciplined defensive display and clinical finishing.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Newcastle 0-2 Man City: Antoine Semenyo scores in semi-final first leg|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cdrexz4r5prt|website=BBC Sport|access-date=2026-01-30|language=en-GB}}</ref> However, the Blues then suffered back‑to‑back defeats. A 2–0 loss away to Manchester United on 17 January marked their first Premier League defeat of 2026, with the hosts scoring twice in the second half to end Manchester City's recent unbeaten run in the derby. Four days later, City were unexpectedly beaten 3–1 by [[FK Bodø/Glimt|Bodø/Glimt]] in the Champions League league phase, as the Norwegian champions capitlized on defensive lapses, and left City needing to win their final league game against [[Galatasaray S.K.|Galatasaray]] to ensure qualification as a top 8 side.

The team responded on 24 January with a much‑needed 2–0 home win over Wolverhampton Wanderers – their first Premier League victory of the year, and Marc Guehi's debut for the club – as Omar Marmoush and  Antoine Semenyo both scored, reducing Arsenal's lead at the top to four points. Their month concluded with a 2–0 home win over Galatasaray on 28 January in the Champions League league phase, ensuring that City qualified for the [[2025–26 UEFA Champions League knockout phase|knockout phase]] last 16 directly as one of the top eight clubs in the standings.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Man City vs Galatasaray: UEFA Champions League 2025/26 League phase|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2046030--man-city-vs-galatasaray/|website=UEFA.com|access-date=2026-01-30|language=en|last=UEFA.com}}</ref>

===Spring period===
Manchester City resumed their Premier League campaign on 1 February with a 2–2 draw away to Tottenham Hotspur. Rayan Cherki and Antoine Semenyo goals gave the blues a two-goal lead at half time, but a second half brace from [[Dominic Solanke]] meant the points were shared. On 8 February, City recorded a significant 2–1 away victory over Liverpool at [[Anfield]]. After falling behind in the second half, Guardiola's side turned the match around with a composed display, as Bernardo Silva slid in with an 84th-minute equalizer before Haaland scored his 20th league goal of the season from the penalty spot in injury time. The result was widely described as a statement performance, keeping City within touching distance of leaders Arsenal in what had become a closely fought title battle.

City then hosted Fulham at the City of Manchester Stadium on 11 February, winning 3–0. A dominant display saw the Blues control possession and territory throughout, with goals from Haaland, Semenyo and Nico O'Reilly securing a comfortable victory and further improving their goal difference. On 22 February, City again hosted Newcastle at the Etihad, with O'Reilly scoring a brace to help the team win 2–1 and keep them in title contentions at the end of the matchweek.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Leeds United vs Manchester City Match Preview & Report {{!}} 2025/2026 {{!}} Premier League |url=https://www.premierleague.com/en/match/2562170 |access-date=2026-04-12 |website=www.premierleague.com |language=en}}</ref>

The month concluded with a 1–0 away victory over Leeds United at [[Elland Road]] on 28 February. Semenyo scored the only goal of the match, and City produced a disciplined defensive performance to secure the three points.

Two league draws at the start of March against relegation threatened Nottingham Forest and West Ham United, looked to have ended City's title race as Arsenal built a 9-point lead at the top of the table

Manchester City's March campaign was dominated by knockout football, beginning with their Champions League round‑of‑16 tie against Real Madrid. On 11 March, City suffered a 3–0 defeat at the Santiago Bernabéu, conceding three in the first half for a [[Federico Valverde]] hat-trick which left them with a significant deficit to overturn in the second leg.

The return fixture on 17 March at the City of Manchester Stadium ended in a 2–1 defeat, with City unable to recover from an early Madrid penalty goal and a red-card for captain Bernardo Silva for deliberate hand-ball, despite briefly reducing the deficit through Erling Haaland. The 5–1 aggregate loss brought an end to City's Champions League campaign at the last‑16 stage.

City responded four days later with a composed performance in the [[2026 EFL Cup final|EFL Cup final]] on 22 March, defeating Arsenal 2–0 at Wembley Stadium. A brace in the second-half from Nico O'Reilly secured the club's first triumph in the competition for five seasons, and Pep Guardiola became the first manager to win the EFL Cup on five occasions.

=== Season run-in ===
Manchester City began April with a dominant 4–0 victory over Liverpool at home in the FA Cup quarter‑final on 4 April. Guardiola's side controlled the match from the outset, combining sustained pressure with clinical finishing, and Haaland's twelfth hat-trick for the club,  to secure a comfortable progression to the semi‑finals. The result extended City's strong domestic cup form and set up a Wembley meeting with [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] later in the month.

City returned to Premier League action on 12 April, after almost a month, with an impressive 3–0 away win over Chelsea at Stamford Bridge. After a balanced first half, City took control early in the second period through goals from Nico O’Reilly, Marc Guéhi and Jérémy Doku. The performance was widely praised for its composure and attacking efficiency, and the victory ensured City remained firmly in contention near the top of the table. At this point they were just 6 points behind the long-time leaders Arsenal with a game in hand, and scheduled due to play them at the Etihad the following weekend.

Manchester City recorded a significant 2–1 win over [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] at the [[City of Manchester Stadium|Etihad Stadium]] on 19 April, narrowing the gap in the title race. City went ahead when [[Rayan Cherki]] scored after a solo run, before Arsenal equalised moments later as [[Kai Havertz]] charged down a clearance from [[Gianluigi Donnarumma]]. The match remained finely balanced until the 65th minute, when [[Erling Haaland]] reacted quickest to a loose ball to restore City's lead. Arsenal struck the woodwork twice in the closing stages, but City held on to secure the victory and move within three points of the league leaders with a game in hand.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McNulty |first=Phil |title=Manchester City 2-1 Arsenal: Erling Haaland scores winner as title race hots up |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/ckg99k2949pt |access-date=2026-04-21 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

City next faced Burnley on 22 April. Haaland scored in the fifth minute from a Jérémy Doku assist, and although City registered nine shots on target, this early goal proved decisive in a 1–0 win. The result confirmed Burnley's relegation to the Championship and briefly took City to the top of the league for the first time since August by the matter of their superior goals scored record. Arsenal would play two more league fixtures before City's next league game.

On 25 April, Manchester City met Southampton—who had eliminated Arsenal in the quarter-finals—at Wembley Stadium for the first FA Cup semi-final of the weekend. [[Finn Azaz]] put Southampton ahead in the 79th minute with a well‑taken strike, but Doku equalised three minutes later with a deflected effort into the bottom-right corner. In the 87th minute, [[Nico González (footballer, born 2002)|Nico González]] scored the winner from outside the penalty area to secure City's place in a record fourth consecutive [[FA Cup final]], where they would face Chelsea, who defeated [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] in the other semi-final.

===End of season===
City then resumed league duties on 4 May with a dramatic 3–3 draw away to [[Everton F.C.|Everton]], twice recovering from deficits through goals from Jérémy Doku and Erling Haaland before Doku equalised deep into stoppage time.<ref>{{cite news |title=Everton 3–3 Manchester City |work=ESPN |date=4 May 2026 |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/match//gameId/713207 |access-date= }}</ref> A comfortable 3–0 home win over [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]] followed on 9 May, with second‑half goals from Doku, Haaland and Omar Marmoush maintaining City's title challenge.<ref>{{cite news |title=Manchester City 3–0 Brentford |work=ESPN |date=9 May 2026 |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/match//gameId/713226 |access-date= }}</ref> City extended their strong run with another 3–0 victory at home to [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] on 13 May, as Antoine Semenyo, Omar Marmoush and Sávio secured a dominant performance that kept Guardiola's side firmly in the race at the top of the table just 2 points behind Arsenal.<ref>{{cite news |title=Manchester City 3–0 Crystal Palace |work=Manchester City FC |date=13 May 2026 |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/man-city-crystal-palace-premier-league-match-report-13-may-2026 |access-date= }}</ref>

Manchester City secured their eighth FA Cup with a 1–0 victory over [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] in the final at Wembley on 16 May, decided by a superb 72nd‑minute flicked finish from Antoine Semenyo after Erling Haaland's low cross from the right.<ref>{{cite news |title=Brilliant Semenyo flick sees off Chelsea to win City an eighth FA Cup |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/man-city-chelsea-fa-cup-final-2026-match-report |work=Manchester City FC |date=16 May 2026 |access-date=22 May 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Manchester City beat Chelsea 1–0 to win 2026 Emirates FA Cup Final |url=https://www.thefa.com/competitions/thefacup |work=The FA |date=16 May 2026 |access-date=22 May 2026}}</ref> The win completed a domestic cup double for City, adding to their League Cup triumph earlier in the season, and marked Pep Guardiola's 20th major trophy with the club.<ref>{{cite news |title=Chelsea 0–1 Man City – FA Cup Final |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-manchester-city/504987 |work=Sky Sports |date=16 May 2026 |access-date=22 May 2026}}</ref>

City's Premier League title challenge ended three days later in a 1–1 draw away to [[AFC Bournemouth|Bournemouth]] on 19 May, a result that confirmed Arsenal as champions with a game to spare. [[Eli Junior Kroupi]] put the hosts ahead in the first half before Haaland equalised in stoppage time, but City were unable to find a winner.<ref>{{cite news |title=Bournemouth 1–1 Manchester City |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/bournemouth-vs-manchester-city/505012 |work=Sky Sports |date=19 May 2026 |access-date=22 May 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Bournemouth vs Manchester City – Final Score |url=https://www.futbol24.com/match/2026/05/19/england/premier-league/bournemouth-vs-manchester-city |work=Futbol24 |date=19 May 2026 |access-date=22 May 2026}}</ref>

On 22 May, after days of press rumours, Manchester City announced that Pep Guardiola would step down as manager at the end of the season, bringing to a close a decade in charge that delivered 20 major trophies and transformed the club's modern era.<ref>{{cite news |title=Guardiola to step down after incredible decade as City Manager |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/pep-guardiola-to-step-down-22-may-2026 |work=Manchester City FC |date=22 May 2026 |access-date=22 May 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Pep Guardiola to leave Manchester City |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/soccer/news/pep-guardiola-to-leave-manchester-city |work=NBC Sports |date=22 May 2026 |access-date=22 May 2026}}</ref> The club confirmed he would continue within the City Football Group as a global ambassador;<ref>{{cite news |title=Pep Guardiola's next job confirmed as he steps down as Man City manager |url=https://pmnewsnigeria.com/2026/05/22/pep-guardiola-next-job-confirmed |location=Lagos, Nigeria|date=22 May 2026 |access-date=22 May 2026|newspaper=[[P.M. News]]}}</ref> and that the newly developed and expanded North Stand at the Etihad Stadium would be named in his honour.<ref>{{cite news |title=North Stand to be renamed "The Pep Guardiola stand" |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/manchester-city-etihad-stand-renaming-63915045 |work=Manchester City FC |date=22 May 2026 |access-date=22 May 2026}}</ref> City lost their final game of the season, and Guardiola's final game in charge, 2–1 to Aston Villa in front of a record attendance of over 63,000 as the new stand was opened for the first time. This game was also marked the final appearances of John Stones and Bernardo Silva for the club. Both had announced they would be leaving on the expiration of their contracts.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Jonathan |title=City beaten in emotional final game for Pep, Stones and Bernardo |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/City%20beaten%20in%20emotional%20final%20game%20for%20Pep,%20Stones%20and%20Bernardo |access-date=2026-05-30 |website=Manchester City FC |language=en}}</ref>

Nineteen current City players were selected for squads participating in the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]], the most for any club in world football and a new record for the expanded competition.<ref>{{cite news |title=Which clubs have the most players at the 2026 World Cup? |work=BBC Sport|date=2 June 2026 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cgkpv6p7yx1o |access-date= 2 June 2026}}</ref>

===FA Cup===
{{main|2025–26 FA Cup}}

As a Premier League side, Manchester City entered the FA Cup in the third round, and were drawn at home to [[Exeter City F.C.|Exeter City]].<ref>{{cite news |title=City discover FA Cup third round opponents |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/man-city-fa-cup-third-round-draw-63900813 |access-date=8 December 2025 |publisher=Manchester City F.C. |date=8 December 2025}}</ref> They were then drawn at home against [[Salford City F.C.|Salford City]] in the fourth round,<ref>{{cite news |title=City's FA Cup fourth round opponents confirmed |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/man-city-fa-cup-fourth-round-draw-2026-63903830 |access-date=13 January 2026 |publisher=Manchester City F.C. |date=12 January 2026}}</ref> away to [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] in the fifth round,<ref>{{cite news |title=City discover FA Cup fifth round opponents |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/man-city-fa-cup-fifth-round-opponent-confirmed-2026-63906862 |access-date=17 February 2026 |publisher=Manchester City F.C. |date=16 February 2026}}</ref> and at home to [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] in the quarter-finals.<ref>{{cite news |title=City to face Liverpool in FA Cup quarter-final |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/man-city-2026-fa-cup-quarter-final-opponents-63908659 |access-date=9 March 2026 |publisher=Manchester City F.C. |date=9 March 2026}}</ref> City then played [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] in the semi-finals at [[Wembley Stadium|Wembley]],<ref>{{cite news |title=City draw Southampton in FA Cup semi-final |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/fa-cup-semi-final-draw-news-63911002 |access-date=5 April 2026 |publisher=Manchester City F.C. |date=5 April 2026}}</ref> and faced [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] in the [[2026 FA Cup final|final]].

===EFL Cup===
{{main|2025–26 EFL Cup}}

As one of the Premier League clubs participating in European competitions, Manchester City entered the competition in the third round, and were drawn away to [[Huddersfield Town A.F.C.|Huddersfield Town]].<ref>{{cite news |title=City to face Huddersfield in Carabao Cup third round |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/carabao-cup-third-round-draw-man-city-learn-opponents-63891907 |access-date=27 August 2025 |publisher=Manchester City F.C. |date=27 August 2025}}</ref> They were then drawn away to [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]] in the fourth round,<ref>{{cite news |title=City to face Swansea in Carabao Cup Fourth Round |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/carabao-cup-fourth-round-manchester-city-63894329 |access-date=24 September 2025 |publisher=Manchester City F.C. |date=24 September 2025}}</ref> and at home to [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]] in the quarter-finals.<ref>{{cite news |title=City to host Brentford in Carabao Cup quarter-final |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/carabao-cup-quarter-final-draw-63897353 |access-date=30 October 2025 |publisher=Manchester City F.C. |date=29 October 2025}}</ref> A two-legged tie against [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] was drawn for the semi-finals, with the first leg being away and second leg at home.<ref>{{cite news |title=Dates and kick-off times confirmed for Carabao Cup semi-final with Newcastle United |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/newcastle-v-manchester-city-carabao-cup-semi-final-dates-confirmed-63901740 |access-date=19 December 2025 |publisher=Manchester City F.C. |date=19 December 2025}}</ref> City then faced [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] in the [[2026 EFL Cup final|final]] at [[Wembley Stadium|Wembley]].
